scope: Tarrant County (Fort Worth, Arlington) - food, housing, utilities, cash_assistance, transportation (plus local LMHA, WIC, workforce, legal, clinics)

records.name: Tarrant Area Food Bank - Find Food
records.description_en: The food bank sends food to a large network of local food pantries. Use its Find Food map to find a pantry near you. It also has senior food boxes, home delivery, mobile food buses, and help applying for SNAP.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Fort Worth and the North Texas area who need food. Each pantry sets its own rules, so call ahead.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Find Food map on the TAFB website to find a pantry, then call the pantry to confirm hours. To get help with a SNAP application, book an appointment with a TAFB Community Resource Specialist.
records.notes: TAFB says it serves 13 counties in North Texas, with other sites in Denton and Weatherford. The main office is a distribution center. Send people to partner pantries using the Find Food map.

records.name: Arlington Charities Food Pantry
records.description_en: A food pantry that gives groceries to people in need in Arlington. It also has a mobile Market Truck, home grocery delivery, help for unhoused neighbors, and a pantry at TCC Southeast.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who live in Arlington zip codes 76001-76019, parts of Grand Prairie (75050-75052, 75054), and Kennedale (76060).

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Arlington zip codes 76001-76019, Grand Prairie 75050-75052 and 75054, or Kennedale 76060

records.how_to_apply: First-time clients should read the First-time Client information on the website. Returning clients can order online.
records.notes: Only certain zip codes are served. The home delivery program is for people who cannot come to the pantry.

records.name: Mission Arlington Emergency Assistance
records.description_en: Free groceries for a few days, clothing, furniture, and household items. It can also help pay part of your rent or a utility bill, give gas vouchers for job interviews, and help you replace an ID.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people and families in crisis in the Arlington area. Help depends on what is available.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the Mission Arlington office during open hours or call (817) 277-6620.
records.notes: Other directories list the office at 210 W. South St., Arlington, but this was not confirmed on the official page. Rent help covers only part of the rent. The official page does not state the service area.

records.name: Meals On Wheels Home-Delivered Meals
records.organization: Meals On Wheels of Tarrant County
records.description_en: Meals delivered to the homes of people who need them. It also offers case management, nutrition counseling, pet meals, and help for veterans.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people living in Tarrant County who need home-delivered meals. Age and homebound rules apply; ask when you call.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the contact form on the website or call. A caseworker will contact you within 3-5 business days.
records.notes: The home page did not list the exact age or homebound rules or any cost.

records.name: Comprehensive Energy Assistance Program (CEAP) - Utility Assistance
records.organization: City of Fort Worth Community Action Partners (CAP)
records.description_en: Helps pay electric, gas, and propane bills. It also offers HVAC repair, some home health and safety repairs, and case management. This is the local CEAP provider for Tarrant County.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Tarrant County residents who meet income limits. If you need utility help, you must be the account holder or an authorized user on the account.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens at 9 a.m. on every other Friday through September. You can also book an in-person appointment; walk-ins are not accepted. Call (817) 392-2276 for help.
records.notes: As of September 2026, CAP listed Emergency Rental Assistance (funds used up), Water Utility Payment Assistance, and Beat the Heat (2026 season over) as unavailable. Online applications open only on certain Fridays, so check the page for the next date. The full list of required documents is in a 'Documents Required' PDF on the page.

records.name: CAP Veterans Assistance
records.organization: City of Fort Worth Community Action Partners (CAP)
records.description_en: Helps veterans pay rent, mortgage, and utility bills. Veterans who live in Fort Worth may also get home changes like wheelchair ramps and grab bars.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For veterans who live in Tarrant County. Home changes are only for veterans who live in Fort Worth.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Tarrant County resident (home modifications: Fort Worth only)

records.how_to_apply: Apply through the CAP online application or book an in-person appointment. Call (817) 392-2276 with questions.
records.notes: The page does not say whether proof of veteran status is needed; ask CAP.

records.name: Rent and Utility Assistance (Tarrant County Community Outreach Fund)
records.description_en: Short-term help paying rent or utility bills for Tarrant County residents. Tarrant County moved its rent and utility help to this nonprofit on November 1, 2025.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Tarrant County residents age 18 or older who are U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents and meet income limits. For example, the limit is $23,475 a year for 1 person and $48,225 a year for 4 people. You must have a disability or work at least 20 hours a week, and you must have no available savings or assets.
records.how_to_apply: Check the Get Help page for application dates, or call or email the Center. Processing can take several weeks.
records.notes: The program page said all available funds had been given out and new funding was expected in October; check before referring. Not for emergencies, because processing takes weeks. Applicants must also apply for SNAP. Tarrant County lists (817) 607-8137 for this program; the Center's main line is (817) 332-6191. The Center also offers child care, Head Start, counseling, benefits enrollment, and financial coaching.

records.name: Presbyterian Night Shelter Emergency Shelter
records.organization: Presbyterian Night Shelter of Tarrant County
records.description_en: An emergency shelter that gives people without a home an overnight bed. It also has residential programs, and the separate True Worth Place day center offers case management and housing help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For anyone without a home, including people with barriers such as a criminal history.
records.how_to_apply: Go to the shelter or call (817) 632-7400. You can also use the Get Help Now page on the website.
records.notes: Secondary directories list intake as 2-4 p.m. and say women with children come to the main door at 5 p.m.; this was not confirmed on the official site. Its website is journeyhome.org.

records.name: True Worth Place Day Shelter
records.organization: Presbyterian Night Shelter of Tarrant County
records.description_en: A day shelter for people experiencing homelessness. It has showers, laundry, lunch, a mailing address, phone and computer use, storage, case management, and job and education programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people experiencing homelessness, including people staying at night shelters or living on the street.
records.how_to_apply: Walk in during open hours or call (817) 289-7474.
records.notes: Daytime only. For an overnight bed, go to Presbyterian Night Shelter, or call the homeless helpline at (817) 996-8800.

records.name: Union Gospel Mission Shelter and Welcome Center
records.organization: Union Gospel Mission of Tarrant County
records.description_en: Shelter, meals, case management, and housing help for people experiencing homelessness. The Welcome Center is the place to start. It is a Christian ministry.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people experiencing homelessness in Tarrant County.
records.how_to_apply: Go to the Welcome Center or call (817) 339-2553.
records.notes: A Fort Worth Report news article says the Welcome Center opened January 20, 2026, and offers housing assessments and help finding a place to stay other than a shelter. The home page does not list its hours.

records.name: Arlington Life Shelter
records.description_en: An emergency shelter and program for people and families experiencing homelessness. It helps people work toward living on their own.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people and families experiencing homelessness. People convicted of a crime against a person in the past 2 years, or of any crime against a child or an older adult, cannot stay.
documents_needed: Two forms of ID, one with a photo (for example, a driver's license, state ID, military ID, passport, student ID, or TB card)
records.how_to_apply: Come during intake hours, 2:00-4:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. Call first to check if a bed is open, because beds are first come, first served.
records.notes: Guests may be given random breath and drug tests.

records.name: Salvation Army Arlington - Family Shelter and Food Pantry
records.organization: The Salvation Army of North Texas
records.description_en: A year-round shelter where families experiencing homelessness can stay together, plus a weekly food pantry and case management. In extreme weather it opens a cooling station and an overnight warming shelter.
records.eligibility_summary_en: The shelter is for families experiencing homelessness. The food pantry is open to the community.
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 860-1836 or visit in person. Call Monday-Friday to book a case management appointment.
records.hours: Food pantry Thursdays 11 a.m.-3 p.m.; case management Mon-Fri by appointment
records.notes: The cooling station opens Mon-Fri 9 a.m.-4 p.m. when the heat index reaches 100 degrees or more. The warming shelter opens on nights below 40 degrees for 4 hours in a row. The source page listed zip 76063, which may be a mistake, so zip is left empty.

records.name: Homeless Helpline / Coordinated Entry
records.organization: Partnership Home (formerly Tarrant County Homeless Coalition)
records.description_en: The main phone line for people who are homeless or about to lose housing. Staff check what you need and connect you to shelter, street outreach, or housing programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Tarrant County who are homeless or in a housing crisis.
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 996-8800 during open hours. Partnership Home's website also has an online housing crisis screening.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-8 p.m.; Sat 10 a.m.-2 p.m.
records.notes: The phone number and hours come from the MHMR Tarrant homeless services page, and True Worth Place also lists this number. Partnership Home's own help page did not show a phone number. Secondary directories say the line also serves Parker County, and that callers can press 5 for street outreach.

records.name: The Archway (formerly SafeHaven of Tarrant County) - Domestic Violence Services
records.description_en: A 24/7 hotline, emergency shelter, housing help, safety planning, services for children, and legal help for people hurt by a partner.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For survivors of domestic or partner violence and their children, mainly in Tarrant County.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24/7 hotline at 1-877-701-7233.
records.notes: The shelter address is not shared publicly. The office line is (817) 535-6462. The old safehaventc.org address now redirects to this site.

records.name: Fort Worth Housing Solutions (Public Housing Authority)
records.description_en: Fort Worth's housing authority. It runs Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8), project-based vouchers, homeless housing programs, affordable apartments, and homebuying help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households. Each program and waitlist has its own rules.
records.how_to_apply: Check the website for waitlists that are open and apply through the online applicant portal. Call (817) 333-3400 with questions.
records.notes: In September 2026 the site showed one open waitlist, for 2-bedroom units at Sedona Village Senior Living (households of 3-4 people). Secondary sources say the main Housing Choice Voucher waitlist is closed. Hearing-impaired callers can use Texas Relay 7-1-1.

records.name: Housing Choice Voucher Program (Section 8) - Arlington
records.description_en: Helps pay rent in private housing for low-income people, older adults, and people with disabilities in Arlington.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Household income must be at or below 50% of the area median income. People who live or work in Arlington get preference. Some criminal histories (felonies, sex offender registration, meth-related) make you ineligible.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online only during the yearly open enrollment period. Applicants on the list can check their status at assistancecheck.com.
records.notes: As of September 2026 the waitlist is NOT open. The last enrollment ran July 31 to August 6, 2025. City pages list different contact details: 501 W. Sanford St. Suite 20 and (817) 275-3351 (2025 news release and Homeless Services page), and 101 W. Abram St. and (817) 459-6777 (HCV page). The city warns people not to give personal information to fake sites claiming the list is open.

records.name: Arlington Homeless Services (Eviction Prevention, Rapid Re-Housing, TBRA)
records.description_en: Arlington programs that help people avoid eviction and help homeless people find housing. Programs include eviction prevention, rapid re-housing, supportive housing, up to 2 years of rent and utility help, and services for young adults ages 18-24.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who live in Arlington with income at or below 50% of the area median income (varies by program). Some programs require an eviction or utility shut-off notice, or that you meet HUD's definition of homeless.
documents_needed: Eviction notice or utility disconnect notice (for some programs)
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 276-6713 or email homelessassistance@arlingtonhousing.us. Eviction prevention applications are taken only on set days, with a limited number each day.
records.notes: The page listed HHSP eviction prevention intake on set Tuesdays (Sept 22 and Oct 6, 8-11 a.m.), with only 50 applications each day. Check the page for current dates.

records.name: Tarrant County Housing Assistance Office (Housing Choice Vouchers)
records.description_en: The county housing authority. It runs Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8) and special voucher programs that help low-income families pay rent.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For extremely low, very low, and low-income families in Tarrant County.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Assistance Connect portal or in person when applications are open. Applicants can check waitlist status online.
records.notes: The line for current participants is (817) 531-7641, and TDD is (888) 444-2122. The office is on the Tarrant County Resource Connection campus. Official pages did not say whether the waitlist is open.

records.name: Trinity Metro Reduced Fare
records.description_en: Lower bus and train fares for older adults, people with disabilities, Medicare card holders, youth, and veterans. You get a reduced fare photo ID card at Fort Worth Central Station.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For seniors 65 and older, people with disabilities, Medicare card holders, youth ages 5-19, and veterans (local tickets only).
documents_needed: Photo ID (Texas ID or driver's license)
Medicare card, Social Security award letter, or VA award letter (disability)
records.how_to_apply: Bring your documents to the Trinity Metro kiosk at Fort Worth Central Station to get a reduced fare photo ID card.
records.hours: Central Station: Mon-Fri 6 a.m.-6 p.m.; Sat-Sun 9 a.m.-6 p.m.
records.cost: Photo ID card $2 (replacement $10); youth one-way fare $1
records.notes: Cards for seniors are good for life. Other cards last 6 months, 1 year, or 2 years. People with disabilities who lack the listed papers must be certified by an approved agency. Secondary sources say people with TANF on a Lone Star Card can get reduced monthly passes, but this was not confirmed on the official page. Children 4 and under ride free.

records.name: Trinity Metro On-Demand Paratransit (ACCESS)
records.description_en: Van rides for people whose disability keeps them from riding the regular bus. You book rides ahead of time.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people with a verified disability that keeps them from using regular buses. You must apply and be approved; approval lasts up to 2 years.
documents_needed: Completed paratransit application (a doctor or agency may need to fill in part of it)
records.how_to_apply: Download the application, fill it out, and turn it in. Approval can take up to 21 days. After you are approved, book rides by calling (817) 215-8600.
records.hours: Reservations 8 a.m.-5 p.m., up to 7 days ahead. Rides from 4:20 a.m. Mon-Sat (6 a.m. Sun) until 11:15 p.m. daily.
records.cost: $4 one-way; 10-ride book $40; personal care attendant rides free
records.notes: Serves Fort Worth and River Oaks only. Book by 5 p.m. the day before your ride. To appeal a decision, call (817) 215-8929.

records.name: Handitran
records.description_en: Door-to-door rides in Arlington for older adults and people with disabilities.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people 65 or older, or people with a disability. If you are under 65, a doctor must confirm your disability.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the Handitran Service Application online and pay a one-time $10 fee. Processing takes up to 3 weeks. Then call (817) 275-3704 to schedule rides.
records.hours: Rides Mon-Fri 7 a.m.-10 p.m., Sat 8 a.m.-9 p.m.; office Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-4:30 p.m.
records.cost: $3 per one-way trip; one care attendant rides free; $10 one-time application fee
records.notes: Serves Arlington and up to 1.5 miles past the city limits. One end of every trip must be inside Arlington. The scheduling line is (817) 275-3704.

records.name: Arlington On-Demand Rideshare
records.description_en: Low-cost shared rides anywhere in Arlington, to the CentrePort TRE train station, and to the Eastchase Parkway area of Fort Worth. Book with an app or by phone.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to anyone.
records.how_to_apply: Book a ride in the Arlington Transportation app or call (817) 784-7382. Pay with a credit card or a prepaid card; prepaid cards can be bought with cash at dollar stores or grocery stores.
records.hours: Mon-Fri 6 a.m.-9 p.m.; Sat 9 a.m.-9 p.m.
records.cost: $3-$8 per trip based on distance; $3 flat to CentrePort
records.notes: The page did not list senior, disability, or low-income discounts. Buying a bundle of ride credits saves money.

records.name: Workforce Solutions for Tarrant County
records.description_en: Free help finding a job, including job listings, computers, resume and interview help, job fairs, and training scholarships. It also runs job programs for people on TANF or SNAP.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to job seekers in Tarrant County. Training and TANF/SNAP job programs have their own rules.
records.how_to_apply: Visit a workforce center or call (817) 413-4000. Use the locations map on the website to find the nearest center.
records.notes: Centers include Arlington, Central, Resource Connection, and Mid-Cities. The Resource Connection center address and phone, (817) 531-5670, come from the Tarrant County Resource Connection directory. TDD/TTY: 1-800-735-2989.

records.name: Child Care Services (Child Care Scholarships) - Tarrant County
records.organization: Child Care Associates for Workforce Solutions for Tarrant County
records.description_en: Helps low-income families pay for child care so parents can work, go to school, or get job training.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Texas families with a child under 13 (or under 19 with a disability) who meet income limits and work, go to school, train, or look for a job. Most families pay part of the cost based on income.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Texas Child Care Connection (TX3C) system. Call Child Care Associates at (817) 831-0374 with questions.
records.cost: Parent share of cost based on income
records.notes: Tarrant County has a long waitlist. Workforce Solutions reported about a 27-month wait, and CCMS said it was pulling families who applied in early 2024. Some priority groups are served sooner. Children must be under 13, or under 19 if they have a disability.

records.name: Tarrant County WIC
records.description_en: WIC gives healthy food, nutrition help, and breastfeeding support to pregnant women, new mothers, babies, and young children.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For pregnant, breastfeeding, and postpartum women, and children under 5, who meet income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 321-5400 to make an appointment at a WIC clinic near you.
records.hours: Call center Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-6 p.m.; clinics Mon-Fri 9 a.m.-1 p.m. and 2-6 p.m., plus one Saturday a month at most clinics
records.notes: Clinics: Arkansas (2596 E. Arkansas Ln, Arlington 76014), Bagsby-Williams (3212 Miller Ave, Fort Worth 76119), Eastside (1100 Bridgewood Dr #116, Fort Worth 76112), Euless (417 W. Euless Blvd, Euless 76040), Green Oaks (2001 S.E. Green Oaks Blvd, Arlington 76018), Haltom City (4113 Denton Hwy 76117), Lake Worth (3800 Adam Grubb, Fort Worth 76135), Resource Connection (2500 Circle Dr Ste 400, Fort Worth 76119), Southside (1101 S. Main St, Fort Worth 76104), Southwest (6551 Granbury Rd, Fort Worth 76133), White Settlement (1638 S. Cherry Ln, Fort Worth 76108). WIC is no longer offered at the Watauga center. The 'pregnant' key was left out because WIC also serves women who are not pregnant.

records.name: MHMR Tarrant Crisis Line and Mental Health Services (Local Mental Health Authority)
records.organization: My Health My Resources (MHMR) of Tarrant County
records.description_en: A 24/7 crisis line you can call or text for a mental health or substance use emergency. MHMR also provides ongoing mental health, addiction, disability, and child services, plus mobile crisis teams.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For children, teens, and adults in Tarrant County.
records.how_to_apply: In a crisis, call or text 1-800-866-2465 at any time. For non-crisis services, call (817) 335-3022.
records.notes: TTY-TDD: (817) 569-4488. Call 911 if someone is in immediate danger. MHMR also runs Liberty House, a 30-bed transitional home for homeless male veterans (admission through the VA).

records.name: JPS Connection (Health Care Financial Assistance)
records.organization: JPS Health Network (Tarrant County Hospital District)
records.description_en: A Tarrant County program that lowers the cost of care at JPS hospitals and clinics, with low co-pays for visits and medicines.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Tarrant County residents with income up to 250% of the federal poverty level. It can also add coverage on top of Medicare or other insurance for people under 250%.
documents_needed: Proof of income (pay stubs or award letters)
Bank statements (self-employed or Social Security recipients)
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the application (in English, Spanish, or Vietnamese) and turn it in with your documents. Apply online, by email to enroll@jpshealth.org, by fax, by mail, or in person at the Enrollment & Eligibility Center.
records.address: 101 W. Allen Ave (JPS Enrollment & Eligibility Center)
records.notes: There are several levels (Connection 1, 2, and 3) based on income. The residency rule is implied by JPS being the county hospital district; confirm with JPS. The enrollment center hours come from the JPS eligibility-enrollment page. Main JPS line: (817) 702-3431.

records.name: North Texas Area Community Health Centers (FQHC)
records.organization: North Texas Area Community Health Centers, Inc.
records.description_en: Community health clinics with primary care for adults and children, women's health, pregnancy support, behavioral health, pharmacy, and vision care. Care is offered to everyone, with payment options for people without insurance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone, including people without insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 625-4254 to make an appointment or to ask for a financial assessment.
records.hours: Beverly Hills: Mon-Thu 7:20 a.m.-7:00 p.m., Fri 7:20 a.m.-6:30 p.m.
records.cost: Payment options for uninsured patients; financial assessment available
records.notes: Other sites: 2909 Mitchell Blvd, Fort Worth 76105 (Mon-Fri 7:40 a.m.-5:00 p.m.) and 1001 N. Waldrop Dr. Suite 708, Arlington 76012 (Mon-Fri 7:20 a.m.-5:20 p.m.).

records.name: Legal Aid of NorthWest Texas - Fort Worth Office
records.description_en: Free civil legal help for low-income people, including eviction and landlord problems, family law, custody, and domestic violence cases.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income people in Tarrant, Erath, Hood, Johnson, Palo Pinto, Parker, and Somervell counties who meet basic eligibility rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 336-3943, ext. 3, during intake hours, call the Legal Aid Line at 1-888-529-5277, or apply online.
records.hours: Phone intake Mon-Wed 8:30-11 a.m. and 1:30-4 p.m.
records.notes: Landlord-tenant hotline: (855) 548-8457. Toll-free: (800) 955-3959. If you have a court deadline or an active lawsuit, call the local office directly.

records.name: 2-1-1 Help Line (Tarrant County)
records.description_en: A free 24/7 phone line that connects you to local help for food, housing, bills, child care, crisis counseling, and more.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone can call.
records.how_to_apply: Dial 2-1-1 from any phone.
records.notes: United Way of Tarrant County runs the local 2-1-1 center as part of the statewide 2-1-1 Texas network. Older adults and people with disabilities can call (817) 258-8125. Veterans can call (844) 489-8387. The address is United Way's office, not a walk-in help center.

records.name: Free Tax Preparation (VITA)
records.description_en: Free help filing your taxes so you can get your full refund and tax credits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For households earning $69,000 or less.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the tax preparation page on United Way's website to find a site or appointment.
records.notes: Mostly offered during tax season. The income limit comes from the United Way home page.

records.name: Area Agency on Aging of Tarrant County
records.description_en: Help for older adults, people with disabilities, and caregivers. Services include free home changes like ramps and grab bars, meals, Medicare and benefits counseling, caregiver support, and nursing home advocacy.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For older adults, people with disabilities, and their caregivers in Tarrant County.
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 258-8125. For meals, call 2-1-1.
records.notes: The page did not state the age limit. Ombudsman line: (817) 258-8102.

records.name: Catholic Charities Fort Worth Services
records.organization: Catholic Charities Diocese of Fort Worth
records.description_en: Help with rides to medical visits, work, and errands, plus low-cost dental care, financial coaching, pregnancy and parenting support, and immigration and refugee services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to people of all faiths. Each service has its own rules.
records.how_to_apply: Call (817) 534-0814 or use the Get Help page to reach the service you need.
records.cost: Varies by service; dental is low-cost
records.notes: Serves the 28-county Diocese of Fort Worth. Secondary sources mention rent and utility help, but the official Get Help page did not list it, so confirm it by phone. Pregnancy support hotline: 1-800-545-5935.

records.name: Tarrant County Resource Connection
records.description_en: A large campus in Fort Worth where many health, job, education, and human service agencies share one location, including the county housing office, Workforce Solutions, and WIC.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Tarrant County residents. Each agency on campus has its own rules.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the campus or call (817) 531-7600. Use the online directory to find the agency you need.
records.notes: The campus is north of I-20, near TCC South Campus, and can be reached by public transit.
